cohort: 16,094 newborns admitted to the NICU of a hospital in the Xiangxi area of China from 2012 to 2020
finding: The prevalence of jaundice and cardiovascular diseases increased over the 9-year study period, while respiratory and neurological diseases decreased, with significant influences from gender, delivery method, gestational age, and birth weight.
mod_finding: Infants born via cesarean delivery had a significantly higher prevalence of neonatal diseases.
birth_weight: Infants of lower birth weight had a higher prevalence of neonatal diseases
